**Tier 3** — derived — a pure function of tier 2 · owned by `analysis` · `public.analysis_runs`

**One row is** One execution of one analysis for one project, identified by the world it ran against (`input_hash`), the parameters it ran with (`params_hash`) and the code that ran (`code_version`). Two runs carrying the same five-part key ARE the same run by definition, which is what makes serving a stored answer sound rather than a bet on how recently a timestamp moved.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `analysis_runs_pkey` |
| `project_id` + `analysis_kind` + `input_hash` + `params_hash` + `code_version` | partial UNIQUE index | `analysis_runs_key_uniq` |

**Natural key:** `project_id` + `analysis_kind` + `input_hash` + `params_hash` + `code_version` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `analysis_runs_key_uniq`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Constraints

These reject the row outright. A value that fails one of them does not arrive
partially or get corrected — the write fails.

|---|---|---|

| `analysis_runs_status_check` | `CHECK (status IN ('running','succeeded','failed'))` | `20260917000006_analysis_store.sql` |

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — all carry a predicate |

Read follows project reachability (`has_project_access`), uuid-only since WP 3.0. `write: null` is a STATEMENT, not an omission: there is no user-facing write path and there must not be one. Every write goes through `analysis_get_or_start`, `analysis_complete_run` and `analysis_fail_run`, each of which takes the actor as a PARAMETER and routes it through `assert_writer_may_act` — so the audit trigger names a person rather than recording `actor_known: false` (G4). There is deliberately NO write policy on this table, which makes `no-tier-skip` (I2) a property of the schema here rather than of today's callers. The RPCs AUTHENTICATE and do not AUTHORIZE: `20260917000005` removed a role gate from the shared preamble after it was found to refuse an organization admin on a live path, and making `min_project_role` load-bearing is D66 and WP 6.2's.

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate row identifier. Carries no meaning — the IDENTITY of a run is the five-column natural key, not this. |
| `project_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The project this analysis ran for. Referenced by uuid and never by a displayable name (`uuid-identity`, G1); cascades on project delete, which is retention rather than mutation of a result. |
| `analysis_kind` | — | `text` | — | — | WHICH analysis ran. Open enum — the CHECK constrains the shape to a lowercase identifier and the catalog of values is the `analysis_kinds` block above, so a new kind costs a sidecar edit and not a migration. |
| `input_hash` | — | `text` | — | — | WP 4.1's `current_graph_hash(project_id)` at the moment the run was claimed: the world this answer is about. This is the anchor invariant `input-hash` (I5) is about — and I5 is NOT met by this table alone, because I5 is about the DERIVED ROW carrying it. WP 4.3 stamps the same value onto the tier-3 rows the analyzers already write. |
| `params_hash` | — | `text` | — | — | SHA-256 of `params` as canonical `jsonb` text. Over jsonb and never over the text a caller sent, because jsonb normalises key order and duplicate keys — so the same parameters written two ways are one cache key rather than two. |
| `code_version` | — | `text` | — | — | WHICH code produced the answer. Part of the key so that a changed analyzer does not serve its predecessor's numbers, and so two versions can coexist on one input hash and be compared (§11's fourth exit check). |
| `params` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | The parameters as sent, beside the hash of them, so a run can be read without reversing a digest. Immutable: re-pointing a stored run at different parameters would re-attribute an answer to a question it never answered. |
| `status` | — | `text` | — | — | `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`. Only a `succeeded` run is ever served as a hit — a `running` row is a claim somebody else is still working on and holds no results, and handing it back would render an empty analysis as a complete one. `failed` sits OUTSIDE the unique index on purpose (see `natural_key_unique`): otherwise the first crash would own that cache key forever and the analysis could never be retried on that input. |
| `started_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the key was claimed. Part of the run's frozen identity, not of its state. |
| `finished_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the run reached `succeeded` or `failed`. Null while running. |
| `duration_ms` | — | `integer` | — | — | Wall-clock milliseconds from claim to finish. Reporting only — nothing keys on it, and a staleness rule that compared it to anything would be the timestamp comparison D12 is about. |
| `row_counts` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | What the run produced, by entity type. Reporting and the Trust Report's input (A3); WP 4.4 assembles it. |
| `warnings` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | The run's own account of its blind spots, carried with the result rather than left in a log — transparency commitment T3, which says every report states the known limits of its own computation. |
| `actor_user_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | WHO asked for this run. NOT NULL, so a run that cannot name its actor cannot exist — the same stance `assert_writer_may_act` takes for the RPC writers (`20260917000005`). Note what attribution means here: the application authenticates against `approved_users` and not Supabase Auth, so the id is CLIENT-ASSERTED (D28) — the database refuses a write into a project the user cannot reach, which is a real constraint, but it is not proof of identity. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | Row insert time, maintained by the database. |
| `updated_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | Last lifecycle change. The IDENTITY columns are frozen by `analysis_runs_identity_is_immutable`; only status, finish and reporting columns move, which is the line between what a run IS and what it is DOING. |
